characters.name: Victoria Barkley
characters.description: Mama Bear: Victoria is very protective of her family and will do what she has to do to protect them. Even if it means shooting a family friend to death or holding a criminal at gunpoint. Non-Idle Rich: Like the rest of her family, Victoria is active in her community, involved in charity work, and is often the first one people go to when there is an issue.

characters.name: Jarrod Barkley
characters.description: Crusading Lawyer: Jarrod has a strong sense of justice, he even takes a case where his own brother is the key witness against his client when he feels that defendant won't get a fair shake otherwise.

characters.name: Nick Barkley
characters.description: Big Brother Instinct: Nick is shown to be protective of his younger sister, Audra, often being suspicious of new men in her life. Nick is also protective of his newly discovered younger brother Heath, after they get through a few bumps, willing to jump into a brawl with any one who has a demeaning comment about Heath's parentage to share. Inverted, in that Nick's protectives also extends to his elder brother Jarrod. Hair-Trigger Temper: Nick is known for his fiery temper. Though he often feels justified in his anger, there are moments were he is shown regretting his hasty actions.

characters.name: Heath Barkley
characters.description: Heroic Bastard: Heath is the result of an affair between Thomas Barkley and Leah Thompson, a woman that lived in the far off mining camp of Strawberry. Some people that learn of his illegitimacy give him a hard time about it, but he doesn't let that stop him from doing the right thing.

characters.name: Audra Barkley
characters.description: Hair of Gold, Heart of Gold: The blonde Audra is a kind and caring soul.

characters.name: Eugene Barkley
characters.description: Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Eugene is initially set up as being another Barkley member who is a chipper medical student. However, he only physically appears in a handful of episodes within the first season and is offhandedly mentioned in a handful of others. After season one, his existence in the story is essentially erased completely. In real life, this is because Eugene's actor, Charles Briles, was drafted into The Vietnam War, but no reasons are given in story as to why his family no longer acknowledges him as a Barkley.

characters.name: Thomas Barkley
characters.description: Posthumous Character: Thomas Barkley died six years before the beginning of the show, but he isn't entirely absent. The actions he did or didn't take in life often wind up affecting his wife, children, and even the town long after his death. One example of this is in "Heritage": Thomas had made a bunch of promises to the minors that worked for him, from comfortable lodgings to schools for their children to discount prices in the mining town's store. As Heath discovers for himself, none of these promises were kept for long or at all: the mining town's current administration has put profit over the working and living conditions of the minors and their families. This bred so much resentment against Thomas specifically that Heath's safety and wellbeing are threatened to the point where one of the residents has to help him sneak out when a group of angry minors come after him during the night. The episode mainly deals with the Barkleys learning about Thomas's broken promises and how to handle them.

characters.name: Silas
characters.description: Old Retainer: Silas apparently single-handedly takes care of the massive Barkley mansion and cooks all the meals, as he's the only servant ever seen. He's also very loyal to the Barkleys, having worked for them a number of years.
